feature_materialization.action: persist query-independent Qwen visual features without changing verifier scores
feature_materialization.finding: The defer-partial-full cost phase survives strict fit/test separation, but the v0 history-rate compiler is not consistently better than first- or second-touch and leaves a future-frequency oracle gap.

retrieval_materialization.finding: Future labels expose strong sparse signed-value headroom, including quality above the complete index, but the fixed qrel-free risk/reuse score does not predict those pages. Naive RRF over incomplete visual support is invalid because it promotes low-value pages merely for ranking highly inside a small subset.

established: Feature reuse and corpus-searchable retrieval materialization are different actions with different quality semantics.
The exact feature state has a measured reuse break-even of about 1.15 future candidate uses per page on both domains.
The marginal retrieval value of visual pages is sparse and signed: a 5% future-label oracle exceeds the corresponding complete z-score hybrid in both held-out test folds.
A sparse visual support cannot inherit the complete index's fixed Top-100 RRF contract.
not_established: The v0 compiler is a paper-quality deployable selector.
Cheap page features and historical locator disagreement predict future signed visual value.
The oracle result transfers to an unseen domain or document-disjoint workload.
The current score-surface replay is an end-to-end system or answer-quality result.
claim_boundary.decision: Retain the two-action state model and measured cost catalog. Replace static global retrieval selection with a query-scope or calibrated signed-value learner; do not tune v0 heuristic weights on the test domains.
